editorial.headline: Engineering Research in Bali: Open Nationally, Dependent on Scope
editorial.standfirst: This engineering and technology R&D activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali eligibility turns on the risk level of the exact scope declared in OSS.
editorial.body:
KBLI 72102 covers regular, systematic research and development in engineering and technology. It embraces engineering and technology research itself, including interdisciplinary work centred principally on natural science and engineering. Its technical territory is expansive: civil and chemical engineering; electrical and electronic systems; environmental, materials and mechanical work; medical, agricultural and instrumentation engineering; and research involving resources, extractive metallurgy and granular mechanics. It also includes nanotechnology, hydrogen, oil and gas, minerals and coal, electricity, and engineering and technology related to meteorology, climatology and geophysics.

The classification is for businesses whose recurring activity is that research and development work. It is open at every stated business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. Nationally, the activity is marked open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is a clear national position for a business conducting the engineering-and-technology R&D described in this scope, rather than a general statement about every activity that may sit around a technical project.

Bali requires a more exact reading. The record does not treat this activity as universally blocked for PMA registration; its Bali status depends on scope. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low- and Medium-Low-risk KBLI activities across the island. At the Large scale, however, OSS risk may be low for some scopes and higher for others. For this activity, PMA registration in Bali is available only by declaring the higher-risk scope.

The practical conclusion is precise rather than pessimistic. Nationally, foreign ownership is open across the listed scales, with a 100% ceiling. In Bali, that national position does not by itself determine whether a proposed registration can proceed. The exact activity must be verified live in OSS, because the declared scope and its risk treatment decide the local PMA outcome. For an engineering R&D business, that distinction belongs at the beginning of the registration analysis, not after the business model has already been framed.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, foreign ownership is open; in Bali, the declared scope and its OSS risk treatment decide the PMA outcome.
